record.original_question: If a nontrivial classical knot is modified by virtualizing some crossings to produce a nontrivial virtual knot with unit Jones polynomial, can the resulting knot nevertheless be classical; can every virtual knot with unit Jones polynomial be related to a classical diagram by virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization; and if two classical knots differ by crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, must they already be classically equivalent?

evidence.quote: Suppose the knot K is classical and not trivial. Suppose that K˜ (obtained from K by virtualizing a subset of its crossings) is not trivial and has a unit Jones polynomial , V (K˜ ) = 1. Is it possible that K˜ is classical (i.e. isotopic through virtual equivalence to a classical knot)?

Suppose K is a virtual knot diagram with unit Jones polynomial. Is K equivalent to a classical diagram via virtual equvalence plus crossing virtualization? Given two classical knots K and K′, if K can be obtained from K′ by a combination of crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, then is K classically equivalent to K′?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the category of virtual knots, i.e. equivalence classes of 4-valent plane graphs whose vertices are decorated either as classical crossings (over/under information) or as virtual crossings, taken modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves (the three classical Reidemeister moves together with the four virtual/mixed moves). The Jones polynomial extends to virtual knots via the Kauffman bracket, and a virtual knot is said to have unit Jones polynomial if its Jones polynomial equals 1.

The operation of crossing virtualization replaces a classical crossing by the same classical crossing flanked on two opposite arcs by virtual crossings; equivalently, it switches the crossing and inserts two virtual crossings. Crossing virtualization preserves the Jones polynomial but is not in general a virtual isotopy. A virtual knot is called classical if it is virtually equivalent to a diagram with no virtual crossings.

Answer the following three questions:

(a) Let K be a nontrivial classical knot, and let K̃ be a virtual knot obtained from a diagram of K by virtualizing some nonempty subset of its classical crossings. Assume K̃ is nontrivial as a virtual knot and that the Jones polynomial of K̃ is 1. Is it possible that K̃ is (virtually equivalent to) a classical knot?

(b) Suppose K is a virtual knot diagram with unit Jones polynomial. Must K be equivalent, via a finite sequence of generalized Reidemeister moves together with crossing virtualizations, to a classical knot diagram?

(c) If two classical knots K and K′ are related by a finite sequence of generalized Reidemeister moves and crossing virtualizations, must K and K′ be classically equivalent (i.e., ambient isotopic as classical knots)?
artifact.status_search_result: These questions, concerning virtual knots with unit Jones polynomial and the crossing-virtualization operation, are listed among the unsolved problems in virtual knot theory. Subsequent introductions and surveys (including Kauffman's "Introduction to Virtual Knot Theory" and follow-up work using the arrow polynomial) continue to present them as open, with no known examples showing that the virtualization of a nontrivial classical knot can be classical, but no proof either way.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to Virtual Knot Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Virtualization produces infinitely many non-trivial virtual knots with unit Jones polynomial; whether these can be classical is unknown.
status_evidence.claim: The status of virtual knots with unit Jones polynomial relative to classical knots is described as open.

status_evidence.title: Derivatives of Jones Polynomials Detect Delta Moves in Virtual Knots
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of virtualization preserving Jones polynomial and the open question of classicality.
status_evidence.claim: Later literature still treats the crossing-virtualization/unit-Jones questions as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Theory – Unsolved Problems
status_evidence.snippet: List includes the questions about virtualizing classical crossings and unit Jones polynomial.
